# meshoptimizer — vendored for Aver

**Upstream:** https://github.com/zeux/meshoptimizer
**Version:** `v1.2` (released 2026-06-30) — pinned to a release tag, not a branch, so a re-vendor
reproduces exactly this code.
**Licence:** MIT, © 2016-2026 Arseny Kapoulkine. `LICENSE.md` is kept beside the sources; removing
it would be a licence violation, and this tree's whole posture (`docs/formats/FORMAT_SPECS.md` §16)
is about not committing those.

## Why it is here

This was **already the engine's choice**, recorded before anything was vendored:

- `docs/rendering/RENDERING.md:42` — "Mesh LOD / meshlets / simplify | meshoptimizer | MIT |
  Nanite-like cluster + LOD backbone"
- `docs/formats/FORMAT_SPECS.md:242` — the `MLET` chunk is "Generated by meshoptimizer
  (`meshopt_buildMeshlets`, MIT) at cook time"
- `docs/formats/FORMAT_SPECS.md:540` and `RENDERING.md:63` list it in the licence tables
- `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:535` recorded it as *absent* — this vendoring is what closes that gap

`Aver.Trifactor` (`modules/trifactor`) is the first and currently only consumer. It uses four
entry points: `meshopt_buildMeshlets` (cluster formation), `meshopt_computeMeshletBounds`
(bounding sphere + normal cone), `meshopt_simplify` with `meshopt_SimplifyLockBorder` (the
boundary-locked simplification that makes the LOD DAG crack-free), and `meshopt_partitionClusters`
(grouping neighbouring clusters before simplifying them as a unit).

The `MLET` limits in `FORMAT_SPECS.md` §5.7 — 64 vertices / 124 primitives — were chosen to match
this library's own shape, so the format and the builder agree without a conversion step.

## What was taken, and what was not

Taken: `src/*.cpp` (20 files), `src/meshoptimizer.h`, `LICENSE.md`.

Deliberately excluded: `demo/`, `tools/`, `js/`, `gltf/`, `extern/`, the upstream `CMakeLists.txt`,
`Makefile` and `CONTRIBUTING.md`. This tree vendors narrowly — see `third_party/stb` and
`third_party/imgui`, which do the same. The excluded directories pull in their own dependencies and
build a gltf converter this engine has no use for; it already has its own importer
(`modules/formats`, `tests/formats/src/ConvertTool.cpp`).

`CMakeLists.txt` here is Aver's own, not upstream's, and lists the sources explicitly for the reason
given in its comment.

## Re-vendoring

    curl -sL https://codeload.github.com/zeux/meshoptimizer/tar.gz/refs/tags/<tag> -o mo.tar.gz
    tar -xzf mo.tar.gz --strip-components=1 -C <tmp>
    cp <tmp>/src/*.cpp <tmp>/src/meshoptimizer.h third_party/meshoptimizer/src/
    cp <tmp>/LICENSE.md third_party/meshoptimizer/

Then update the version above, and check whether upstream added or removed a `src/*.cpp` — the
explicit source list in `CMakeLists.txt` will not notice on its own.
